chunks: Ahmad ibn al- mad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us by reading, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, saying: I was at the place of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

and a man entered and asked him about a man who did not know whether he prayed one [rak'ah] or two, so he said to him: He must repeat the prayer. Then he said to him: Then where is what has been narrated that the jurist does not repeat the prayer? He said: That is only with regards to the third and fourth [rak'ah].
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who is unsure if they prayed one or two units of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* clarifies a specific jurisprudential nuance regarding *shakk* (doubt) in prayer, distinguishing between the general principle of leniency for the *faqih* (jurist) and its specific application to the number of rak'ahs. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies that the exemption from re-prayer applies to uncertainty between three and four units, whereas uncertainty between one and two necessitates repetition, reflecting the Shia methodology of precise textual interpretation (*ta'wil*) over generalization. This distinction highlights the scholarly rigor in applying hadiths to avoid legal ambiguity in daily worship.
